about: Rule and threshold table for the pipe-clog module (key clog). Kept inside this package on purpose: rubric JSONs in src/cascade/rubrics are fingerprinted by drift.py. Tags: PUBLIC = quoted from a public rule or paper (URL given); team-proposed = our design choice, validate before use; Assumption = modelling assumption with no source.

BACKFLOW_ANNUAL.meaning: Backflow prevention assemblies inspected and tested at least annually, by a certified Backflow Prevention Assembly Tester licensed by the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health; test records kept at least three years.
BACKFLOW_ANNUAL.quote: All approved backflow assemblies shall be inspected and tested annually or more frequently if determined to be necessary by this Department.

FOG_25PCT.meaning: Grease interceptors of food service establishments (FSEs) cleaned often enough that combined FOG and solids never exceed 25% of total liquid depth, with a cleaning logbook. Applies only if the tower has an FSE under a LASAN Industrial Wastewater Permit.
FOG_25PCT.quote: Grease interceptors shall be cleaned at a frequency such that the combined FOG and solids accumulation does not exceed 25% of the total liquid depth of the grease interceptor.
FOG_25PCT.source: LA Sanitation Sewer System Management Plan v3.0 (25 Jan 2019), section 7.5.3

GREASE_TRAP_DAILY.meaning: Grease TRAPS (small under-sink or hydromechanical units, as distinct from interceptors) cleaned and visually inspected daily.
GREASE_TRAP_DAILY.quote: Grease traps shall be cleaned on a daily basis.
GREASE_TRAP_DAILY.source: LA Sanitation Sewer System Management Plan v3.0, section 7.5.3

FOG_PROGRAM.meaning: LAMC 64.30: food service establishments need an Industrial Wastewater Permit, best management practices and an approved grease removal device; cooling grease hardens in pipes and causes spills.
FOG_PROGRAM.source: LA Sanitation and Environment, Fats, Oils and Grease (FOG) program page

CCTV_48H_AFTER_OVERFLOW.meaning: Camera-inspect a drain within about 48 hours after any backup or overflow. This is LASAN's practice for CITY sewer pipes, adopted here as a team-proposed rule for building drains; no building-drain rule was found.
CCTV_48H_AFTER_OVERFLOW.quote: usually within 48 hours after the initial occurrence of an overflow
CCTV_48H_AFTER_OVERFLOW.source: LA Sanitation SSMP v3.0 (city sewer practice)

PERFORMANCE_HISTORY.meaning: LASAN sets each city sewer's cleaning frequency primarily by its performance history and previous cleaning findings; we mirror this by shortening intervals after backups.
PERFORMANCE_HISTORY.quote: determine primarily by its performance history and previous cleaning findings

UPC_608_2_PRV_80PSI.meaning: Static pressure above 80 psi needs an approved pressure regulator preceded by an adequate strainer, reducing static pressure to 80 psi or less. EXCEPTION: regulators of 1-1/2 in (40 mm) or larger do not require a strainer, so a strainer at a riser-size zone PRV is a design choice, not a code mandate. Where one is fitted, its differential pressure at test flow is the most direct check. Verified only in the UPC-based Hawaii 2021 text; California Plumbing Code equivalence is unverified.
UPC_608_2_PRV_80PSI.quote: Pressure regulator(s) equal to or exceeding 1 1/2 inches (40 mm) shall not require a strainer.
UPC_608_2_PRV_80PSI.source: Section 608.2 Excessive Water Pressure (Hawaii Plumbing Code 2021, UPC-based, UpCodes)

DN100_STACK_MAX_LPS.meaning: Maximum drainage flow for a DN100 stack is 4.0 L/s with square branch entries and 5.2 L/s with swept entries (EN 12056-2 / DIN 1986-100, as summarised by Lansing 2023). A test draw sent to a DN100 stack must stay at or below 4.0 L/s; above that it must go to a break tank or cistern.
DN100_STACK_MAX_LPS.quote: The maximum drainage flow permitted for a DN 100 (4 inch) stack is 4.0 L/s (63 gpm) ... If swept branch connection fittings are used, the maximum drainage flow is increased to 5.2 L/s

ACTIVE_TEST_LPS.meaning: Nightly active flow test: one motorised test-draw valve at the top of each pressure zone opens for one short step at a known flow (4.0 L/s, and 2.5 L/s as the stack-safe variant). Cerebro only PROPOSES the schedule; a facilities person approves the standing schedule; the BMS runs it with a BMS-side low-pressure abort. Domestic cold water only, never fire, sprinkler or standpipe piping.

ACTIVE_TEST_SECONDS.meaning: Proposed hold time of each test draw, logged at 1 s and averaged once the flow has settled (research verifier's recommendation, to limit the water used per night). The simulation does NOT model this window: EPANET solves the settled flow at one 10-minute step, and the transient after the valve opens is not simulated. The pressure-noise assumption applies to the averaged reading.

PRESSURE_NOISE_M.meaning: Pressure transducer noise per reading (10-min or test-window mean). No datasheet checked.

FLOW_NOISE.meaning: Clamp-on transit-time flow meter accuracy: +-1.0% of reading from 0.5 to 12 m/s and +-0.0046 m/s below 0.5 m/s. Modelled as sd = max(1% of Q, 0.0046 m/s x pipe area).
FLOW_NOISE.quote: +-1.0% of reading from 1.5 to 40 ft/sec (0.5 to 12.0 m/sec) and +-0.015 ft/sec (+-0.0046 m/sec) for velocity below 1.5 ft/sec
FLOW_NOISE.source: AW-Lake CUTT clamp-on ultrasonic flow meter page

K_BANDS.meaning: Clog severity classes are contiguous bands of the extra minor-loss coefficient K (drawn log-uniform from 1 to 300). The mapping from K to a physical blockage (percent area, scale, debris) is unsourced.

MINOR_LOSS.meaning: EPANET models minor losses as h = K v^2 / 2g and pipe friction by Hazen-Williams (C 130-140 for new cast iron).

FALSE_ALARM_TARGET.meaning: Alarm thresholds are set on OUT-OF-FOLD predictions for clean training nights at their 95th percentile, never on the held-out test weeks.

PERSISTENCE_2_OF_3.meaning: A clog work order is proposed only when 2 of any 3 consecutive nightly tests alarm.

PAIRED_DOWN_DROP.meaning: Paired drain rule: upstream level above its predicted normal AND downstream level below 70% of its trailing 7-day median.

LEVEL_NOISE_M.meaning: Drain level sensor noise (sd 0.5 cm) and 1 cm logging step; the 1 cm step mirrors the Bellinge iFix note that level is stored only on changes over 1 cm.
LEVEL_NOISE_M.quote: to save space data is stored only if the value difference is more than 1 cm for level sensors

DRAIN_TEST.meaning: Known-volume nightly drain-down test: 150 L discharged into the stack at 2.5 L/s (below the 4.0 L/s DN100 stack limit), level logged at the cleanout; drain-down time compared with the commissioning value.

DRAIN_RATIO_BANDS.meaning: Drain-down ratio 1.2 or more: schedule camera inspection; 2.0 or more, or no drain-down within the test window: urgent work order.

CAMERA_BASE_INTERVAL.meaning: Default camera (CCTV) interval for stack bases and the building drain. No authoritative fixed interval for building drains was found; shortened by risk and after backups, mirroring LASAN's performance-history approach.

STRAINER_BASE_INTERVAL.meaning: Default strainer inspection interval at PRV stations where a strainer is fitted; brought forward to 7 days when the nightly flow test alarms on the strainer location on 2 of 3 nights. In our model a clean strainer's head loss at test flow is below the noise of two gauge-pressure sensors, so the check is 'alarm vs no alarm', not a ratio to commissioning.
